overall_summary: Most content centers heavily around 'self respect' with low absolute view counts, ranging mostly between 3 to 41 views. A notable outlier is the mother-themed video ('माँ जब पूछती है') hitting 196 views, suggesting a wider emotional resonance outside strict romantic/self-respect micro-moments. However, to respect the channel's core identity while capitalizing on higher-performing relatable real-life emotional touchpoints, we should blend self-respect with universal relational bonds.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on concrete phone actions like status lists (41 views), pinned chats (41 views), and archived folders (23 views) consistently outperform abstract emotional whining.
winning_patterns.action: Continue anchoring scripts in hyper-specific, modern smartphone or daily micro-habits.

winning_patterns.pattern: Broad family or unconditional emotional bonds
winning_patterns.evidence: The stray 'Maa' video hit 196 views, vastly outperforming all romantic self-respect shorts.
winning_patterns.action: Reserve a small experiment budget to test universal emotional expressions beyond romantic heartbreak.

weak_patterns.pattern: Generic late-night solitude or vague overthinking hooks
weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'रात के दो बजे' (13 views) and 'मेज पर रखी चाय' (6 views) show lower engagement compared to specific boundary-setting actions.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid vague ambient night/tea tropes without an active choice or tangible item attached.
